The following steps are important control steps to ensure that the mRNA levels of the transfected constructs are equal. Only samples that pass this control step will be selected for the Jess assay. The readers are welcome to perform the total RNA isolation and qPCR using standard protocol established in their labs. Here we provide an example of our procedure that combines several standard protocols from different vendors.5.Isolate total RNA from the samples in RNA Blue (Top-bio) stored at −80°C.Note: Top-bio manufacturer’s protocol is available here: https://www.top-bio.com/img/uploaded/639_PLen-RNA-Blue-rev-012022.pdfOptional: Using GlycoBlue Coprecipitant during the total RNA isolation will help to better visualize the RNA pellets.6.Perform a digestion step with the TURBO DNA-free Kit (Invitrogen).Note: Invitrogen TURBO DNA-free Kit protocol is available online: https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2F1907M_turbodnafree_UG.pdfOptional: For the DNase treatment, it is possible to use 0.8 U (units) of the TURBO DNase Enzyme for 20 μL RNA samples with concentrations in the range of 1–5 μg (measured with, for example, NanoDrop) and then incubate the samples for one hour at 37°C followed by termination of the reaction with 2 μL of DNase Inactivation Reagent.7.Use equal amounts of total RNA, e.g., 0.5 μg per each sample, to synthesize cDNA using High-capacity cDNA reverse Transcription Kit and RNase Inhibitor (Applied Biosystems). Incubate the reactions for 10 min at 25°C, followed by 120 min at 37°C and 5 min at 85°C, with a subsequent temperature drop to 4°C to allow the samples to be used for the next steps.Note: Instructions on the usage of High-capacity cDNA reverse Transcription Kit are here: https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2FMAN0017977_highcap_cDNA_RT_UG.pdfOptional: Add spike RNA to 20 μL of each reaction before cDNA synthesis to control the efficiency of the cDNA synthesis step. We routinely use for this purpose 1 μL of yeast S. cerevisiae RPL41 RNA with a concentration in the range of 0.5–1 ng/μL.8.For 10 μL qPCR reactions, mix HOT FIREPol EvaGreen qPCR Mix Plus, 5× (Solis BioDyne) (data sheet is available here: https://solisbiodyne.com/pics/9800_DS-08-25_v3_HOT_FIREPol_EvaGreen_qPCR_Mix_Plus_no_ROX_revised_12.04.2022.pdf), cDNA and 0.03 μL of 300 nM forward primer and 0.03 μL of 300 nM reverse primer (either those described in the associated research paper or in the current protocol in key recourses table (KRT)). Run qPCR using an appropriate program, an example of which can be found in Table 1.Optional: Using the Bio-Rad CFX384 Real-Time PCR system will allow for multiple constructs to be efficiently validated and compared in a single qPCR run; an example of such a qPCR plate is shown in Figure 3A (upper part).Note: To compare ATF4-HA expression levels between WT and mutant constructs, a reverse primer matching the HA tag should be used to eliminate interference by the endogenous ATF4 mRNA.CRITICAL: To control for the same transfection efficiency, primers corresponding to the plasmid region encoding neomycin/kanamycin resistance should be included for each pair of constructs being compared in each experiment, as well as controls for RNA isolation (18S rRNA primers) and cDNA synthesis efficiency (yeast RPL41 primers), as summarized in KRT. Primer efficiency has to be tested prior to the actual Real-Time PCR experiment. The PCR efficiency has to be determined for both the hATF4-HA tag and the controls, the threshold crossing point (Ct) values must be linearly correlated with the logarithmic value of the cDNA amount (ln cDNA) for the slope of this line to inform the PCR efficiency at the given parameters. An example of a representative experiment for each primer pair used in this protocol (hATF4-HA tag, Neomycin, 18S, yeast RPL41) is shown in Figure 3A (bottom part), where the template was used in several dilutions for reactions (ln cDNA) and the obtained Ct values were plotted to a graph. steps.title: Order and receive HEK293T cryovial
steps.instruction: Order a cryovial of frozen HEK293T cells from a supplier (e.g., ATCC) and receive it for the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare sterile workspace and pre‑warm media
steps.instruction: Sterilize the Class II biological safety cabinet (Thermo Scientific) with UV light, pre‑warm high‑glucose DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS to 37 °C in a water bath, and pre‑fill a 60.1 cm² tissue‑culture dish (Dish 100) with 10 mL of the pre‑warmed medium.

steps.title: Thaw frozen HEK293T cells quickly
steps.instruction: Wear cryogenic gloves, transfer the cryovial from liquid‑nitrogen storage to the cell‑culture room, and place it in a 37 °C water bath for approximately 2 minutes to thaw rapidly, minimizing DMSO exposure.

steps.title: Seed thawed cells and grow to confluence
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette with a sterile filter tip, add the thawed cell suspension to the pre‑filled Dish 100 containing 10 mL medium, then incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until the culture reaches ~80 % confluence.

steps.title: Passage cells and count
steps.instruction: Passage the 80 % confluent cells to a new Dish 100 with 10 mL fresh medium and grow to ~80 % confluence; during passage, wash cells with warm PBS, digest with 0.025 % trypsin in PBS for 5 min, neutralize with medium, and count cells using a Corning Cell Counter (Life Sciences, 6749) as per the vendor’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Obtain the ATF4‑HA plasmids (order or create), transform into competent bacteria, plate on LB agar containing the appropriate antibiotic (e.g., kanamycin or neomycin) and incubate 16 h at 37 °C; then inoculate single colonies into LB broth with the same antibiotic and shake‑incubate 16 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Isolate and purify plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate plasmid DNA with the QIAGEN Plasmid Mini Kit following the manufacturer’s handbook, elute the DNA in 50 µL UltraPure distilled water, then further purify using the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit to reduce toxicity and improve transfection efficiency.

steps.title: Adjust plasmid concentration
steps.instruction: Measure plasmid concentration on a NanoDrop One and dilute each plasmid to an equal concentration of 450–500 ng/µL; use freshly prepared plasmid for each experiment to maximize transfection efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare thapsigargin stock solution
steps.instruction: Order thapsigargin (Tg) and dissolve the powder in DMSO to make a 1 mM stock solution; store the stock protected from light.

steps.title: Seed cells in six‑well plates
steps.instruction: Seed pre‑grown HEK293T cells into a six‑well plate (Techno Plastic Products) at 2.5 × 10⁵ cells per well in 2.5 mL complete DMEM, preparing a total of 24 wells (≈6 × 10⁶ cells per well).

steps.title: Transfect cells with plasmid DNA
steps.instruction:
Twenty‑four hours after seeding (cells at 50–70 % confluence), prepare 12 transfection reactions (each serving two paired wells):
1. Add 1 mL serum‑free DMEM to a 1.5 mL tube.
2. Add 5 µg plasmid DNA (2.5 µg per well) and vortex.
3. Add 10 µL TurboFect (Thermo Fisher), vortex again, and incubate 20 min at 23 °C.
4. Add 0.5 mL of the reaction dropwise to each paired well.
Include a positive control (WT construct) and a negative control (no plasmid).

steps.title: Treat cells with thapsigargin or DMSO
steps.instruction:
Eight hours post‑transfection, treat half the wells with Tg (final 1 µM) and the other half with DMSO control:
1. Prepare two 15 mL tubes each containing 6.5 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS.
2. To the Tg tube add 45.5 µL of the 1 mM Tg stock; to the DMSO tube add 45.5 µL DMSO; vortex each.
3. Add 0.5 mL of the appropriate master mix dropwise to each well according to the pairing scheme.
Incubate for 3 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Harvest cell lysates for Jess assay
steps.instruction:
After the 3‑h treatment, aspirate media from three wells at a time to avoid drying, then add 200 µL 1× Glo Lysis Buffer (Promega) supplemented with protease inhibitors (pre‑warmed to 23 °C for 30 min) to each well; repeat for all wells.
Incubate plates in an Eppendorf Thermomixer Comfort 5355 at 550 rpm, 25 °C for 5 min.
Collect lysates into pre‑labeled, pre‑chilled microcentrifuge tubes on ice using a 1 mL filter tip, vortex, and centrifuge 5 min at 16,000 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare lysate aliquots and RNA samples
steps.instruction:
Transfer 180 µL supernatant from each tube to a new chilled tube on ice.
From this, aliquot four × 20 µL portions for the Jess assay and flash‑freeze them in liquid nitrogen.
Transfer 90 µL of supernatant to a pre‑chilled 1.5 mL RNase/DNase‑free tube and add 750 µL RNA Blue reagent (Top‑Bio, Trizol alternative).
Store all lysate and RNA‑Blue samples at –80 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Isolate total RNA from stored samples
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from the RNA Blue samples stored at –80 °C using the Top‑Bio RNA Blue protocol (manufacturer’s PDF). Optionally add GlycoBlue coprecipitant to improve pellet visibility.

steps.title: Digest RNA with TURBO DNase
steps.instruction: Treat the isolated RNA with the TURBO DNA‑free Kit (Invitrogen): for each 20 µL RNA sample (1–5 µg), add 0.8 U TURBO DNase, incubate 1 h at 37 °C, then terminate the reaction with 2 µL DNase Inactivation Reagent.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from RNA
steps.instruction: Use 0.5 µg of DNase‑treated RNA per 20 µL reverse‑transcription reaction with the High‑capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems) plus RNase Inhibitor. Incubate 10 min at 25 °C, 120 min at 37 °C, 5 min at 85 °C, then hold at 4 °C. Optionally add 1 µL yeast RPL41 RNA (0.5–1 ng/µL) as a spike‑in control.

steps.title: Set up and run qPCR
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 µL qPCR reactions containing HOT FIREPol EvaGreen qPCR Mix Plus 5× (Solis BioDyne), cDNA template, 0.03 µL of 300 nM forward primer and 0.03 µL of 300 nM reverse primer (HA‑tag primer for ATF4‑HA, neomycin/kanamycin resistance primer, 18S rRNA primer, and yeast RPL41 primer as controls). Run the program listed in Table 1. Include WT, no‑plasmid, and technical replicates. Verify primer efficiencies (≥ three 10‑fold cDNA dilutions, Ct difference ≤ 1 cycle).

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data
steps.instruction: Analyze the qPCR results with Bio‑Rad CFX Manager, confirming that control primer efficiencies meet criteria and that Ct values are within the acceptable range before proceeding.

steps.title: Install and open Compass software
steps.instruction: Ensure the latest release of Compass for SW (Simple Western) software is installed on both the Jess instrument computer and the analysis PC, then open the Jess run file in the software.

steps.title: Verify run summary and standards
steps.instruction: In the Run Summary tab, review the separation video and IV plot for bubbles; then select the Standards menu and confirm the presence of the three fluorescent standard peaks (Std1, Std29, Std230) from the 5× Master Mix.

steps.title: Check ladder and sample peaks
steps.instruction: Select Samples, verify that the Ladder (capillary 1) shows six peaks at 12, 40, 66, 116, 180, and 230 kDa, and confirm that each sample (capillaries 2‑25) displays a single peak in the chemiluminescence channel.

steps.title: Validate chemiluminescence signal range
steps.instruction: Ensure the chemiluminescent signal for each sample falls between 3 000 and 90 000 U; discard any sample outside this range.

steps.title: Overlay PN channel and assess loading
steps.instruction: Overlay the chemiluminescence channel with the fluorescent PN channel; verify that the PN Corr. Area for each sample is > 22 000 U (upper limit ≈ 45 000 U). Discard samples that do not meet this criterion.

steps.title: Normalize and name target peak
steps.instruction: Set the normalization region to 12–220 kDa and change the Area End value to 180 kDa. Name the target peak corresponding to ATF4‑HA (≈ 53 kDa); if the automatic fit is poor, manually adjust Peak Fit parameters (Threshold from 10 to 9.0 or 8.0; Width from 9.0 to 8.0 or 7.0).

steps.title: Compare WT and mutant peak areas
steps.instruction: Select all sample capillaries, enable the PN channel, set the WT sample as the reference (100 % PN loading), and discard any sample whose PN loading differs by more than 20 % (i.e., > 120 % or < 80 %). Record the corrected peak‑area values for the ATF4‑HA target peak to compare expression between WT and mutant constructs.
